incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGE OPENED - Sev2 - Smart routing / fallback loop detected. Pager: @Lee (oncall). Channel: #incidents. Thread started 1752406789

Sam W: seeing a big uptick in 5xx and elevated latency from hosted API since ~10:12 UTC. Error spike correlates with smart-routing rollout 10:05. Customers reporting partial failures (esp. eu & apac). Paging oncall.

Lee (oncall): on it. grabbing logs now. Noted: fallback policy configured to prefer lower-cost variant in eu region when capacity limited. Might be mistakenly matching more requests than intended.

Maria P: I can pull routing config. grabbing routing policy json

Maria P: ```
{
  "policy_id": "smart-fallback-v2",
  "rules": [
    {"match": "region:eu*", "fallback": "region:us-west-2,model:redwood-7b-quant"},
    {"match": "latency>200", "fallback": "model:redwood-13b-quant"}
  ],
  "enable": true
}
```

Alex G: hmm looks like the region match is greedy (eu*), and our EU pool was reporting degraded capacity at 10:04 -> policy started sending traffic to us-west-2. But us-west-2 pool has a model variant mismatch (13b vs 7b) and KV cache incompatible -> some requests error, triggering fallback back to EU -> loop.

Sam W: logs show repeated "fallback-invoked" -> "route-change" -> "fallback-invoked" for same request IDs. example:

Sam W: ```
[10:13:21] req=abcd1234 fallback-invoked from eu-central-1 -> us-west-2 (model redwood-7b-quant)
[10:13:22] req=abcd1234 execution-error: kv-cache-incompatible
[10:13:22] req=abcd1234 fallback-invoked from us-west-2 -> eu-central-1 (model redwood-13b-quant)
[10:13:24] req=abcd1234 rate-limit-exceeded
```

Nate: oh bad. So policy allowed cross-variant fallbacks which caused cache/format mismatches and errors, then further fallbacks triggered again. That creates a routing loop and increases load across pools.

Lee (oncall): quick mitigation options: 1) disable smart-fallback policy 2) force-route all EU traffic to EU pool (force-region) 3) rollback to prior routing snapshot. Which is safest? I'm leaning disable policy first.

Maria P: disabling policy will stop fallbacks but won't remove already queued/batched requests. Also some customers pinned to 13b might get degraded latency if EU pool still congested.

Alex G: we tried a temporary force-region override to eu to stop cross-region traffic earlier (command below). It reduced cross-region chatter but caused increased 429s in eu because capacity was saturated.

Alex G: ```bash
rwdctl routing override --scope=customer --region=eu-central-1 --force=true --reason="stop cross-region loop"
```

Sam W: noted. After that override at 10:22, eu latencies climbed and 10% of calls returned 429s for a few minutes. Customers A & C reported degraded service.

Lee (oncall): I'm going to open bridge and escalate to eng-runtime and infra. Need someone to take dedicated capacity or temporarily scale EU pool.

Alex G: scaling EU pool up by adding 2x nodes now. ETA 3m. Also clearing KV cache on EU nodes for compatibility.

Nate: important: do NOT rollback routing snapshot blindly. A previous rollback we attempted earlier (10:18) to older policy restored an older rule that forced model redwood-7b on all traffic -> caused mix of 7b inference calls to endpoints expecting 13b outputs and broke downstream validators. That's what triggered more customer errors.

Lee (oncall): thanks. So current playbook: 1) disable smart-fallback policy (Maria will do) 2) scale EU pool + clear KV cache (Alex) 3) lift force-region override only after capacity stabilizes 4) confirm error rates drop then optionally reintroduce safer fallback rules behind a canary.

Maria P: disabling policy now. Command:

Maria P: ```bash
deploy-bot disable-policy --id=smart-fallback-v2 --actor="Maria P"
```

deploy-bot: policy smart-fallback-v2 disabled by Maria P at 10:27:03 UTC

Alex G: EU pool scaled + KV cache cleared at 10:30 UTC. Observing CPU/GPU load stabilizing.

Sam W: error rate dropping from 7.2% -> 1.1% over 5m. Latency almost back to baseline.

customer-ops-bot: Noted customer impact window 10:05-10:30 UTC. Affected customers: AcmeCorp (10% requests 503/429), FinTrack (sporadic errors), BetaTest orgs. Logging contact attempts for proactive outreach.

Lee (oncall): I'm going to remove the force-region override at 10:34 to let routing return to normal once EU capacity confirmed.

Alex G: override removal command:

Alex G: ```bash
rwdctl routing override remove --id=override-eu-force --actor="Alex G"
```

deploy-bot: override override-eu-force removed by Alex G at 10:35:12 UTC

Sam W: monitoring. Error rate down to 0.4%. No new fallbacks being logged.

Nate: post-incident action items (quick):
- tighten match rules (avoid greedy eu*), add variant compatibility checks before fallback
- add cooldown on cross-region fallbacks to prevent loops
- alert when fallback rates exceed threshold
- add canary rollout for routing policy changes
- document safe rollback steps (don't automatically restore old rules without compatibility checks)

Lee (oncall): handing off to Day Eng for follow-up. I'm on-call authoring postmortem. @Maria P @Alex G @Nate please add timelines and commands to the incident doc.

Maria P: acknowledged. I'll add the policy diffs and the exact command history.

Sam W: customers reached out via support; CSMs notified. We should offer credits to impacted ones (cc finance).

customer-ops-bot: Outreach list created. Slack thread #customer-impact-1752406789 linked.

Lee (oncall): closing page. If error rate spikes again reopen. Great work team. :heart:
